goal: Build pycparser to satisfy the complete public pure-Python C99 parser specification.

atoms.title: Pure-Python tokenize, parse and regenerate pipeline
atoms.input: After the offline install, tokenize 'int main(void) { return 0; }' with CLexer, parse it with pycparser.CParser().parse, and pass the result to pycparser.c_generator.CGenerator().visit.
atoms.expected: The text is tokenized, parsed into a c_ast.FileAST and regenerated as a C string that re-parses without error; only standard-library modules are imported.
gaps: '~50 node types' is approximate; section 2 enumerates 49 node classes.

atoms.title: No third-party runtime dependencies
atoms.input: Inspect the installed distribution's declared runtime requirements and import pycparser, c_ast, c_parser, c_lexer and c_generator in an interpreter that holds only the standard library and the pre-baked build backend; record every top-level module they import.
atoms.expected: No runtime dependency is declared, every pycparser module imports, and every module imported from outside the pycparser package belongs to the Python standard library.

atoms.title: Offline editable install via setup.sh
atoms.input: Run the project's setup.sh in the pinned image with networking disabled and no package index, then import pycparser from an unrelated working directory.
atoms.expected: setup.sh completes without network access and without installing new packages, producing an editable install built with the pre-baked setuptools/wheel backend; the import resolves to the project source tree.
gaps: The text says setup.sh builds and installs the project 'for you'; it does not state whether the candidate authors or may modify setup.sh and pyproject.toml.
Whether build isolation must be disabled is not stated; only that the build runs fully offline.

atoms.title: Public import surface
atoms.input: Execute the five import statements of the Package Structure block in a fresh interpreter.
atoms.expected: All succeed: pycparser exposes CParser and c_ast; pycparser.c_ast exposes NodeVisitor; pycparser.c_generator exposes CGenerator; pycparser.c_lexer exposes CLexer and Token; pycparser.c_parser exposes Coord and ParseError.

atoms.title: Top-level CParser re-export
atoms.input: import pycparser and pycparser.c_parser; compare pycparser.CParser with pycparser.c_parser.CParser.
atoms.expected: pycparser.CParser is the same object as pycparser.c_parser.CParser.

atoms.title: parse returns FileAST and records the filename
atoms.input: p = CParser(); a = p.parse('int x;'); b = p.parse('int x;\nint y;', filename='m.c').
atoms.expected: Both calls return c_ast.FileAST instances; a.ext[0].coord.file == '<unknown>' (the default filename); the Decl for y in b has coord.file == 'm.c' and coord.line == 2.

atoms.title: Variable, function and K&R declarations
atoms.input: Parse 'int x, *p; extern int g(int, char *); int kr(a, b) int a; char b; { return a; }'.
atoms.expected: No ParseError. Decl nodes named x (type TypeDecl) and p (type PtrDecl) exist; g is a Decl with storage ['extern'] whose type is a FuncDecl with a two-entry ParamList; kr is a FuncDef whose param_decls is a list of two Decls named a (int) and b (char) and whose body is a Compound.
gaps: Whether 'int x, *p;' yields two separate FileAST.ext entries or another grouping is unspecified.
How the K&R identifier list appears in FuncDecl.args is unspecified.

atoms.title: Multi-word specifiers, qualifiers and declarator chains
atoms.input: Parse 'unsigned long long int a; const volatile char c; _Atomic int t; int *p; int m[3][4]; int (*fp)(int, double);'.
atoms.expected: a's IdentifierType.names == ['unsigned', 'long', 'long', 'int']; c carries the 'const' and 'volatile' qualifiers and t carries '_Atomic'; p's type is PtrDecl -> TypeDecl; m's type is ArrayDecl (dim Constant '3') whose type is ArrayDecl (dim Constant '4') whose type is a TypeDecl; fp's type is PtrDecl whose type is a FuncDecl with two parameters. Each chain ends in a TypeDecl whose declname is the declared name.
gaps: Declarator nesting order is not spelled out; it is derived from C declarator semantics.

atoms.title: Struct, union and enum with bit-fields, flexible and anonymous members
atoms.input: Parse 'struct S { unsigned a : 3; union { int i; float f; }; char data[]; }; enum E { A, B = 2 };'.
atoms.expected: Struct S has three member Decls: a with bitsize Constant '3'; a nameless member whose type is a Union with two members; data whose type is an ArrayDecl with dim None. Enum E's values is an EnumeratorList holding Enumerator A without a value expression (value None) and Enumerator B with value Constant '2'.

atoms.title: Designated initializers and compound literals
atoms.input: Parse 'struct P { int x, y; }; struct P p = { .y = 2, .x = 1 }; int a[4] = { [2] = 5, 6 }; int *q = (int []){ 1, 2 };'.
atoms.expected: p.init is an InitList of two NamedInitializer nodes whose name lists designate y and x and whose expr values are Constants '2' and '1'; a.init is an InitList whose first element is a NamedInitializer designating index 2 with expr Constant '5' and whose second element is Constant '6'; q.init is a CompoundLiteral whose type is a Typename and whose init is an InitList of Constants '1' and '2'.
gaps: The node class used for a designator inside NamedInitializer.name (field vs index designator) is not specified.

atoms.title: Expression precedence and comma operator
atoms.input: Parse 'int f(int a, int b, int c) { int x; x = a + b * c; x = a || b && c; x = a - b - c; x = (a, b, c); x = a ? b : c; x = (char)a << 1; return x; }'.
atoms.expected: No ParseError. The rvalues are, in order: BinaryOp '+' whose right is BinaryOp '*'; BinaryOp '||' whose right is BinaryOp '&&'; BinaryOp '-' whose left is BinaryOp '-' (left associativity); an accepted comma expression (its node shape is fixed by R05.22); a TernaryOp; BinaryOp '<<' whose left is a Cast.

atoms.title: All statement kinds
atoms.input: Parse 'int f(int n) { int i; if (n) i = 1; else i = 2; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) continue; while (n) break; do n--; while (n); switch (n) { case 1: n = 2; break; default: n = 3; } goto end; end: return n; }'.
atoms.expected: No ParseError. The body Compound contains an If with non-None iffalse, a For whose stmt is Continue, a While whose stmt is Break, a DoWhile, a Switch whose statement contains Case and Default nodes, a Goto with name 'end', and a Label named 'end' whose stmt is a Return.

atoms.title: C11 keywords: _Static_assert, _Alignas, _Noreturn, _Atomic, _Pragma
atoms.input: Parse '_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, "int size"); _Alignas(16) int buf; _Noreturn void die(void); _Atomic int a; _Atomic(int) b; _Pragma("once")\nint z;' at file scope.
atoms.expected: No ParseError. A StaticAssert node has cond BinaryOp '==' and a string Constant message; buf's Decl.align holds one Alignas node; die's funcspec contains '_Noreturn'; '_Atomic' appears in the qualifiers of a and of b; a Pragma node is among the file-scope items.
gaps: Where _Pragma may appear (file scope, statement position) is not stated.
Whether the _Static_assert message is optional is not stated.

atoms.title: Variable-length arrays and array parameter qualifiers
atoms.input: Parse 'void f(int n, const int a[const n]) { int v[n]; }'.
atoms.expected: Parameter a's type is an ArrayDecl with dim ID 'n' and dim_quals ['const']; local v's type is an ArrayDecl with dim ID 'n'.

atoms.title: #line directives update Coord
atoms.expected: a.coord has file 'orig.c' and line 1; b.coord has file 'gen.c' and line 100; c.coord has file 'gen.c' and line 101.
gaps: Numbering after #line (the next source line becomes N) follows the C standard; the text only says file/line are updated.
Whether the linemarker form '# N "file"' or #line without a filename is accepted is not stated.
Handling of other preprocessor directives such as #include is not stated; inputs are assumed preprocessed.

atoms.title: Empty external declaration
atoms.input: Parse ';' and 'int x;;\n;'.
atoms.expected: Neither raises ParseError; the second result still contains the Decl for x.
gaps: Whether an empty declaration adds an entry to FileAST.ext is unspecified.

atoms.title: Scoped typedef/identifier disambiguation
atoms.input: Parse 'typedef int T; int a, b; void f(void) { T * x; a * b; { int T = 3; T = T + 1; } T * y; }'.
atoms.expected: 'T * x;' and 'T * y;' are Decls of x and y whose type is PtrDecl -> TypeDecl -> IdentifierType names ['T']; 'a * b;' is an expression statement BinaryOp '*'; inside the inner block T is an ordinary variable: a Decl named 'T' of type int and an Assignment whose lvalue is ID 'T'.

atoms.title: Dollar sign in identifiers
atoms.input: Parse 'int a$b; int $x = 1; int y$;' and lex 'a$b $x' with a CLexer whose type lookup returns False.
atoms.expected: Decl names are 'a$b', '$x' and 'y$'; the lexer yields exactly two ID tokens with values 'a$b' and '$x'.

atoms.title: Coord attributes and string form
atoms.input: Parse 'int x;' with filename='c.c'; read the Decl's coord.file, coord.line, coord.column and str(coord).
atoms.expected: coord.file == 'c.c' and coord.line == 1; str(coord) == 'c.c:1' when column is unset and 'c.c:1:<column>' when column is set.
gaps: Whether the parser populates column, and its numbering base, is unspecified.
The Coord constructor signature and what counts as an unset column (None vs 0) are not documented.

atoms.title: Node base class and coord attribute
atoms.input: Walk every node reachable through children() from the AST of 'int f(int a) { return a; }'.
atoms.expected: Every node is an instance of c_ast.Node and its coord is a Coord or None; the FuncDef's Decl carries a Coord.

atoms.title: children() tuple with indexed sequence names
atoms.input: Parse 'int a; int b; void f(void) { a = 1; b = 2; }'; call children() on the FileAST and on the function body Compound.
atoms.expected: Both return tuples of (name, node) pairs: names 'ext[0]', 'ext[1]', 'ext[2]' for the FileAST and 'block_items[0]', 'block_items[1]' for the Compound, in source order.

atoms.title: attr_names is a class-level tuple of leaf names
atoms.input: Read attr_names on the classes c_ast.ID, c_ast.BinaryOp, c_ast.Constant and c_ast.Decl without instantiating them.
atoms.expected: Each is a tuple; ID.attr_names == ('name',); BinaryOp.attr_names == ('op',); set(Constant.attr_names) == {'type', 'value'}; Decl.attr_names contains none of its child names type, init, bitsize.
gaps: The order of names inside a multi-name attr_names tuple is not stated.

atoms.title: show() pretty-printer options
atoms.input: For the AST of 'int x = 1;' parsed with filename='s.c', call show(buf=io.StringIO()) with defaults, then separately with attrnames=True, nodenames=True and showcoord=True.
atoms.expected: Default output names FileAST on its first line, deeper nodes are more indented, and it contains neither 'ext[0]' nor 's.c:1'; attrnames=True output includes the leaf value x; nodenames=True output includes 'ext[0]'; showcoord=True output includes 's.c:1'.
gaps: Exact line format, indent width and attribute rendering of show() are unspecified.

atoms.title: Nodes iterate over their children
atoms.input: list(iter(node)) for the FileAST and the Compound from R05.02's input.
atoms.expected: Yields the child node objects themselves (not (name, node) pairs), the same objects children() returns.
gaps: Iteration order is not stated explicitly; children() order is the natural reference.

atoms.title: Mutable nodes enable AST rewriting
atoms.input: Parse 'int f(int a, int b) { return a + b; }', set the return expression's left ID .name = 'c', generate with CGenerator and re-parse the output.
atoms.expected: The assignment succeeds and is reflected in the output: the re-parsed return expression is BinaryOp '+' with left ID 'c' and right ID 'b'.

atoms.title: Programmatic AST construction feeds CGenerator
atoms.input: CGenerator().visit(c_ast.FileAST([c_ast.Decl('x', [], [], [], [], c_ast.TypeDecl('x', [], [], c_ast.IdentifierType(['int'])), c_ast.Constant('int', '5'), None)])) with no parse step.
atoms.expected: Returns C text whose stripped form is 'int x = 5;'.

atoms.title: JSON serialization via children() and attr_names
atoms.input: A generic function maps each node to a dict holding '_nodetype' (class name), each attr_names value, each children() child as a nested dict, and 'coord' as str(coord); apply it to the AST of 'int x = 1;' parsed with filename='j.c' and pass the result to json.dumps.
atoms.expected: json.dumps succeeds; the root dict has _nodetype 'FileAST'; the nested Decl dict has _nodetype 'Decl', name 'x', and coord 'j.c:1' (with ':column' appended only when the column is set).
gaps: How sequence children are keyed in the dict (e.g. 'ext[0]' versus a list under 'ext') is not specified.

atoms.title: Node class inventory with __slots__
atoms.input: For each of the 49 class names listed under Declarations, Statements, Expressions and Other, getattr(c_ast, name).
atoms.expected: Every class exists, subclasses c_ast.Node and defines __slots__.
gaps: Whether __slots__ must prevent arbitrary new attributes (no __dict__ anywhere in the hierarchy) is not stated.

atoms.title: Positional/keyword constructors with keyword-only coord
atoms.input: Build c_ast.IdentifierType(names=['int']) and c_ast.IdentifierType(['int']); build a Decl by keyword (name='x', quals=['const'], align=[], storage=['static'], funcspec=['inline'], type=t, init=None, bitsize=None) and with the same values positionally; build c_ast.ID('x', coord=co) and attempt c_ast.ID('x', co).
atoms.expected: Keyword and positional forms set identical attribute values; coord= sets node.coord; passing coord positionally raises TypeError.

atoms.title: Declaration-family attribute order and child/leaf split
atoms.input: Construct FileAST, Decl, TypeDecl, IdentifierType, PtrDecl, ArrayDecl, FuncDecl, FuncDef, Typedef, Struct, Union, Enum, Enumerator, EnumeratorList, ParamList, EllipsisParam, DeclList and Typename positionally with a distinct value per listed attribute (a node for each * name, a list of nodes for each ** name).
atoms.expected: Each positional argument lands on the attribute named at that position in the table; children() yields every non-None * attribute under its own name and each element of a ** list as 'name[i]'; attr_names holds exactly the unmarked names; EllipsisParam takes no attributes and has no children.
gaps: Omission of None-valued children from children() is only implied (line 119: empty parens add no child node).
align is listed unmarked (leaf) yet holds Alignas nodes per line 125; whether those nodes also appear in children() is unspecified.

atoms.title: Statement, expression and other node attributes
atoms.input: Construct every node from Compound through Alignas in the table positionally with a distinct value per listed attribute.
atoms.expected: Each positional argument lands on the attribute named at that position; Break, Continue and EmptyStatement take no attributes; Goto.name, Label.name, BinaryOp/UnaryOp/Assignment.op, Constant.type/value, ID.name, StructRef.type and Pragma.string are in attr_names; NamedInitializer.name and every ** name yield indexed children; other starred names yield named children when non-None.
gaps: Pragma.string is listed in attr_names but may hold a Constant node (line 124).

atoms.title: BinaryOp and Assignment operator strings
atoms.input: Parse a function body containing 'x = a + b; x = a * b; x = a || b; x = a && b; x = a == b; x = a >> b; x += a; x *= a; x >>= a;'.
atoms.expected: BinaryOp.op values are '+', '*', '||', '&&', '==', '>>'; Assignment.op values are '=' (for each plain assignment), '+=', '*=', '>>='.

atoms.title: UnaryOp operator strings
atoms.input: Parse the expressions '&a', '*p', '-a', '!a', 'a++', 'a--', 'sizeof a' and 'sizeof(int)' inside a function body.
atoms.expected: UnaryOp.op is '&', '*', '-', '!', 'p++', 'p--', 'sizeof' and 'sizeof' respectively.
gaps: The op spelling for prefix ++/-- is not given; only postfix 'p++'/'p--' is.
The node shape of sizeof(type-name) beyond op 'sizeof' is not stated.

atoms.title: StructRef access kind
atoms.input: Parse 's.f' and 'p->f' inside a function body.
atoms.expected: StructRef.type is '.' and '->' respectively; name is the base expression (ID 's' / ID 'p') and field identifies member f.

atoms.title: Constant kind and source text
atoms.input: Parse initializers 42, 0x2A, 10u, 10L, 3.14, 2.5f, 1.0L, "hi" and 'c'.
atoms.expected: Constant.value is the exact source text ('42', '0x2A', '10u', '10L', '3.14', '2.5f', '1.0L', '"hi"', "'c'"); Constant.type is 'int', 'int', 'unsigned int', 'long int', 'double', 'float', 'long double', 'string' and 'char' respectively.
gaps: The type string for combined or doubled suffixes (UL, LL, ULL) is not given, and 'appended' conflicts with the examples 'unsigned int'/'long int' on word order.
Constant.type for wide string/char literals is not stated.

atoms.title: Unsized and flexible array dim is None
atoms.input: Parse 'extern char buf[]; struct M { int n; char data[]; }; int k[4];'.
atoms.expected: buf and data have ArrayDecl.dim None; k has ArrayDecl.dim Constant '4'.

atoms.title: Empty parameter and argument lists
atoms.input: Parse 'int f(); int g(void); int h(int a); void t(void) { f(); h(1); }'.
atoms.expected: f's FuncDecl.args is None and its children() has no args entry; g's args is a ParamList with exactly one Typename whose type names void; h's args is a ParamList; the call f() has FuncCall.args None and h(1) has an ExprList holding one Constant.

atoms.title: Struct/union body states and bit-field width
atoms.input: Parse 'struct A; struct B {}; struct C { int x : 4; int y; }; union U;'.
atoms.expected: A.decls is None; B.decls == []; C.decls is a list of two member Decls where x.bitsize is Constant '4' and y.bitsize is None; U.decls is None.
gaps: An empty struct body is not standard C99; acceptance is implied by the decls == [] rule rather than stated as a grammar extension.

atoms.title: TypeDecl interposition rule
atoms.input: Parse 'int x; struct S { int a; }; struct S s; typedef struct rec { int v; } rec_t; enum E { A }; struct F; struct G { struct { int q; }; }; int n = sizeof(struct { int z; }); struct S *ps;'.
atoms.expected: x: Decl.type is TypeDecl(declname 'x') over IdentifierType; s: TypeDecl(declname 's') over the Struct; rec_t: Typedef.type is TypeDecl(declname 'rec_t') over the Struct; the standalone struct S, enum E and forward struct F are Decls with name None whose type is the Struct/Enum directly; G's anonymous member is a Decl with name None whose type is a Struct directly; the sizeof operand's Typename has a TypeDecl over the Struct; ps: PtrDecl over TypeDecl over the Struct.

atoms.title: quals, storage and funcspec are string lists
atoms.input: Parse 'static const int a = 1; extern volatile int b; static inline int f(void) { return 0; } _Noreturn void g(void);'.
atoms.expected: All three attributes are Python lists of str: a has storage ['static'] and quals containing 'const'; b has storage ['extern'] and quals containing 'volatile'; f has storage ['static'] and funcspec ['inline']; g has funcspec ['_Noreturn'].

atoms.title: Comma operator represented as ExprList
atoms.input: Parse 'int f(void) { int x; x = (1, 2, 3); return x; }'.
atoms.expected: The assignment's rvalue is an ExprList whose exprs are Constants '1', '2', '3' in order; no BinaryOp with op ',' appears.

atoms.title: Pragma.string for operator and directive forms
atoms.input: Parse '_Pragma("pack(push, 1)")\nint x;' and '#pragma once\nint y;'.
atoms.expected: The first Pragma.string is a Constant whose value == '"pack(push, 1)"' (quotes included); the second Pragma.string is a plain str containing 'once'.
gaps: Whether the #pragma directive text includes the 'pragma' keyword or surrounding whitespace is not stated.

atoms.title: _Alignas captured as Alignas nodes and re-emitted
atoms.input: Parse '_Alignas(16) int a; int b;' and generate C from the AST.
atoms.expected: a's Decl.align is a list holding one Alignas whose alignment is Constant '16'; b's Decl.align == []; the generated text contains '_Alignas(16)' for a.
gaps: Whether the same Alignas node also appears on the declaration's TypeDecl.align is not stated.

atoms.title: Source-order specifier words and _Atomic spelling
atoms.input: Parse 'unsigned long long int a; long unsigned b; volatile const int e; int _Atomic c; _Atomic(int) d;'.
atoms.expected: a's names == ['unsigned', 'long', 'long', 'int']; b's names == ['long', 'unsigned']; e's Decl.quals == ['volatile', 'const']; '_Atomic' appears in a quals list for c and for d.

atoms.title: Qualifier placement on simple declarations
atoms.input: Parse 'const int a; int const b; _Atomic int c; int _Atomic flag; const _Atomic(int) x;', then generate C and re-parse it.
atoms.expected: Decl.quals of a contains 'const' and of x contains 'const' and '_Atomic'; TypeDecl.quals contains 'const' for a and b and '_Atomic' for c, flag and x; after generate -> re-parse, flag's TypeDecl.quals still contains '_Atomic'.
gaps: Whether a trailing qualifier (int const b) or a bare leading _Atomic (_Atomic int c) also appears in Decl.quals is not stated.

atoms.title: Leading qualifiers on pointer and array declarations
atoms.input: Parse 'const volatile int *p; const volatile int a[3];'.
atoms.expected: p: PtrDecl.quals contains neither 'const' nor 'volatile' while PtrDecl.type (TypeDecl).quals contains both; a: ArrayDecl.type.quals contains both and ArrayDecl.dim_quals contains neither.
gaps: Whether Decl.quals also carries these leading qualifiers in the pointer/array case is not stated.

atoms.title: Visitor dispatch and recursive generic_visit
atoms.input: class V(NodeVisitor) with only visit_ID, which appends node.name; V().visit(CParser().parse('int f(int a) { return a + g(a); }')).
atoms.expected: Recorded names == ['a', 'g', 'a']: nodes without a visit_ method (FileAST, FuncDef, Compound, Return, BinaryOp, FuncCall, ExprList, ...) are traversed by generic_visit and every ID reaches visit_ID in children() order.

atoms.title: Handled nodes are not auto-recursed
atoms.input: Parse 'void f(void) { g(a); b; }'. Visitor A defines visit_FuncCall (records 'call', no generic_visit) and visit_ID (records the name); visitor B is identical except its visit_FuncCall then calls self.generic_visit(node).
atoms.expected: A records ['call', 'b']; B records ['call', 'g', 'a', 'b'].

atoms.title: CLexer construction and token stream
atoms.input: lex = CLexer(error_func, on_lbrace, on_rbrace, lambda name: False); lex.input('int x;\nx = 42;'); call lex.token() until it returns None.
atoms.expected: Every result before the end is a Token with type, value, lineno and column attributes; the stream starts with INT 'int' then ID 'x'; the INT_CONST_DEC token has value '42' and lineno 2; token() then returns None.
gaps: Column numbering base, whether a separate build step precedes input(), and when on_lbrace_func/on_rbrace_func fire are unspecified.
The error_func call signature is not documented.

atoms.title: Keyword, operator and literal token types
atoms.input: Lex 'int void return if while for struct enum typedef switch case default sizeof static extern const volatile + - * / % && || == != <= >= << >> -> ++ -- ... 42 0x2A 052 0b101 3.14 0x1.8p1 "s" 'c' L"w" L'w' name'.
atoms.expected: Token types in order: INT VOID RETURN IF WHILE FOR STRUCT ENUM TYPEDEF SWITCH CASE DEFAULT SIZEOF STATIC EXTERN CONST VOLATILE, PLUS MINUS TIMES DIVIDE MOD LAND LOR EQ NE LE GE LSHIFT RSHIFT ARROW PLUSPLUS MINUSMINUS ELLIPSIS, INT_CONST_DEC INT_CONST_HEX INT_CONST_OCT INT_CONST_BIN FLOAT_CONST HEX_FLOAT_CONST STRING_LITERAL CHAR_CONST WSTRING_LITERAL WCHAR_CONST, ID.
gaps: Names of assignment-operator and punctuation tokens are not listed ('assignment ops', 'etc.').

atoms.title: type_lookup_func selects TYPEID
atoms.input: CLexer whose type_lookup_func records each call and returns name == 'T'; lex 'T x; U y;'.
atoms.expected: Identifier tokens are TYPEID 'T', ID 'x', ID 'U', ID 'y'; the lookup was called for each of 'T', 'x', 'U' and 'y'.

atoms.title: Generator API and conventional formatting
atoms.input: CGenerator().visit(CParser().parse('int x=5;int f(void){x=x+1;return x;}')) and CGenerator().visit(c_ast.ID('x')).
atoms.expected: The first call returns a str containing 'int x = 5;' and 'x = x + 1;'; visiting the ID node alone returns 'x'.

atoms.title: Default full parenthesization
atoms.input: Parse 'void f(void) { x = p * q * r; y = a + b * c; }' and generate with CGenerator().
atoms.expected: Output contains 'x = (p * q) * r;' and 'y = a + (b * c);': every binary operand that is itself a binary expression is parenthesized and the assignment right-hand side is not.

atoms.title: reduce_parentheses omits only redundant parentheses
atoms.input: Parse 'void f(void) { x = p * q * r; y = a + b * c; z = (a + b) * c; w = a - (b - c); }' and generate with CGenerator(reduce_parentheses=True).
atoms.expected: Output contains 'x = p * q * r;' and 'y = a + b * c;' while keeping 'z = (a + b) * c;' and 'w = a - (b - c);'.

atoms.title: Round-trip fidelity in both modes
atoms.input: Inside a function body, parse statements using '- -x', 'a - (b - c)', '(a = b) + 1', '(char)(a + b)', 'a ? b : (c ? d : e)', '*p++', '(*p)++', 'sizeof(int) * 2' and 'f((a, b))'; generate with reduce_parentheses False and True; re-parse each output.
atoms.expected: Every generated text is valid C that re-parses without error to an AST equal to the original when compared by node class, attr_names values and children() names (coord ignored).
gaps: The equality relation behind 'the same AST' (coord excluded) is not defined in the text.

atoms.title: ParseError on structural errors with file:line prefix
atoms.input: Parse with filename='bad.c' each of: 'int x = 1\nint y;' (missing ;), 'int f(void) {' (unclosed brace), 'int x; )' (stray token).
atoms.expected: Each raises pycparser.c_parser.ParseError whose str starts with 'bad.c:<line>: ' followed by a non-empty description; for the single-line stray-token case the prefix is 'bad.c:1: '.
gaps: The description wording and the line reported for an error detected at end of input or on the next line are unspecified.
ParseError's base class is not stated.
Whether the message includes a column when the Coord has one is not stated.

atoms.title: Invalid type-specifier combinations rejected
atoms.input: Parse separately 'int int x;', 'char double y;', 'void int z;' and the legal 'unsigned long long int w;' and 'long double d;'.
atoms.expected: The three illegal declarations raise ParseError; the legal ones parse with IdentifierType.names ['unsigned', 'long', 'long', 'int'] and ['long', 'double'].
gaps: The full set of illegal combinations beyond duplicated or conflicting base types (e.g. 'long long long', 'signed unsigned') is left to the C standard.

integration.scenario: Round-trip a feature-rich translation unit through CGenerator in both parenthesization modes.
integration.input: One translation unit combining a K&R definition, multi-word specifiers, pointer/array/function-pointer declarators, a struct with bit-field, anonymous union and flexible array member, an enum, designated initializers, a compound literal, every statement kind, _Static_assert/_Alignas/_Noreturn/_Atomic, and a VLA with an array-parameter qualifier.
integration.expected: For reduce_parentheses False and True the generated text re-parses without ParseError, and the re-parsed AST equals the original when compared by node class, attr_names values and children() names (coord ignored).

integration.scenario: Rewrite a parsed AST with a NodeVisitor, then regenerate and re-parse.
integration.input: Parse 'int f(int a, int b) { int t = a * b; return t + a; }'; a NodeVisitor whose visit_ID renames 'a' to 'b' and whose visit_BinaryOp changes op '*' to '+' and then calls self.generic_visit(node); generate with CGenerator() and re-parse.
integration.expected: The output re-parses; t's init is BinaryOp '+' over ID 'b' and ID 'b'; the return expression is BinaryOp '+' over ID 't' and ID 'b'; the parameter Decls are still named a and b because they are not ID nodes.

integration.scenario: Construct a function definition programmatically and generate it without parsing.
integration.input: Build 'int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }' as FuncDef(Decl('add', ..., FuncDecl(ParamList([Decl a, Decl b]), TypeDecl('add', [], [], IdentifierType(['int']))), None, None), None, Compound([Return(BinaryOp('+', ID('a'), ID('b')))])), mixing positional and keyword arguments and passing coord=None by keyword; generate with CGenerator().
integration.expected: The generator returns C text that re-parses to an AST equal to the constructed one when compared by node class, attr_names values and children() names (coord ignored).

integration.scenario: Serialize a parsed AST to JSON using only children() and attr_names.
integration.expected: The round-tripped JSON has root _nodetype 'FileAST'; child entries follow children() names; each node dict carries its attr_names values; a's coord string is 'j.c:1' and nodes after the directive carry 'gen.c:<line>' coords (':column' only when set); the Pragma's string serializes as a nested Constant dict whose value is '"pack(push, 1)"'.

integration.scenario: Track a typedef name through the lexer hook, parser scopes and generator.
integration.input: Text 'typedef int T; void f(void) { T * x; { int T = 0; T * 2; } T * y; }': parse with CParser, generate and re-parse; separately lex it with a CLexer whose type_lookup_func returns name == 'T'.
integration.expected: The parser yields Decls x and y of PtrDecl type and a BinaryOp '*' for 'T * 2;' in the inner block; the regenerated text re-parses to an equal AST; the scope-free lexer labels every T token TYPEID, showing the parser's scoped lookup drives disambiguation.
